method: Line is modelled as concentric layers wound on the spool. Each layer adds one line diameter to the wound radius and holds spool width divided by line diameter turns at its mean diameter, discounted by the winding density for loose, criss-crossed laying (85% by default). The capacity is the sum of those layer lengths from the arbor to the fill line, which is the lip diameter less twice the fill gap because the gap is radial. A line thicker than the radial fill depth cannot be wound. For the two-line plan the braid goes on first and the topshot last: the interface diameter where a band of the requested topshot length ends exactly at the fill line is found by bisection, and the braid backing is the fill of the band from the arbor to that diameter. If the topshot does not fit even on the bare spool, the plan reports the largest topshot the spool holds instead of inventing a backing length. Measurements come from the reel itself, and published capacities assume a fuller spool, so results are planning estimates rather than a replacement for the maker's rating.
